chunks: "Panelization means arranging multiple copies of a board, or sometimes different boards, into one bigger panel that's manufactured and assembled together.
The fab does it anyway on its production panel, but I also design an assembly array so the shop can run it through the SMT line as one unit. It helps for a few reasons.
Small boards are hard to handle on conveyors, so you add rails with tooling holes and fiducials.
Paste printing, placement and reflow then process N boards in one pass, which cuts cost per board. And you use laminate more efficiently.
The boards are held together either by V-scores, which are grooves cut from both sides leaving a thin web you snap at the end, or by routed tabs with perforations, which people call mousebites.
V-score is cheap and fast but only works for straight lines and boards that touch, and it needs component keep-out near the cut.
Tabs allow odd shapes and gaps between boards, but you get small stubs on the edge to clean up.
I also keep sensitive parts like ceramic capacitors away from the breakout area, because snapping a panel flexes the board."
